decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already extends bowl removal and cleaning access to retail food-service and sanitation contexts; the established bowl-removal behavior needs no additional value change.
The existing same-message MODIFY captures the retail context but omits the explicit requirement to separate liquids from electrical components.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Larry, The latest updates are looking great. Seeing the plumbing, drainage routing, bowl integration, and overall structure come together has me even more excited about where this is heading. As I’ve been thinking ahead, one thing that keeps coming to mind is the possibility of eventually using the Matcha Mixer in a retail location if we move forward with opening a shop. Because of that, I wanted to start thinking about food-service and health department considerations early while we’re still in the prototype stage. A few things I’d love to keep in mind as the build progresses: 
 Food-contact materials (stainless steel, food-grade plastics, food-grade silicone, etc.) Ease of cleaning and sanitation Making sure there aren’t any hidden areas where liquid can collect or become trapped Easy removal of bowls, whisks, and components for cleaning Separation between liquids and electrical components Accessibility for maintenance and servicing if something ever needs to be replaced When you get a chance, I’d also love to know what materials are being used in the food-contact areas and whether there are any areas you see as potential sanitation or cleaning challenges. Long term, I think it would be helpful to keep documentation on: 
 materials used CAD files wiring layout cleaning procedures exploded-view drawings if available Not because we need all of that right now, but because if this evolves into something bigger, having that information could be incredibly valuable. Overall, everything is looking fantastic and I’m really excited to see the testing videos and final assembly. It’s amazing seeing the project move from an idea into a real machine. 

Karla Burton

value_updates.liquid_electrical_separation: Liquids must be separated from electrical components.

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already extends the established maintenance and replacement access requirement to the food-service context.
Sanitation, trapped-liquid prevention, and component cleanability do not change the valve operation, button interaction, or controlled-flow behavior.
The source adds sanitation considerations but does not change the spout's geometry, orientation, downward pour direction, or existing stainless-steel construction.
The request to retain possible future documentation does not reopen the approved BOM or require a new component-selection decision at this stage.
The source explicitly requires the whisks to be easy to remove for cleaning, adding a cleanability constraint to the whisk configuration.

decisions.reason: Considering future food-service sanitation does not change the current V1 priority or the approved custom-spout sourcing policy.
The sanitation decision does not alter the platform height, cup clearance, platform configuration, or mixer fit.
Food-service and sanitation considerations do not change any branding, wording, placard placement, or logo requirement.
The source does not change the required matcha texture, foam consistency, or high-speed mixing quality.
Although sanitation and splash control both concern cleanliness, the source does not modify the established splash target or mitigation methods.
